title: Compactifiable comparison of correspondence six-operation diagrams
statement:
Use the finite coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $c:C\to X\times_kX$ and $\bar c:\bar C\to\bar X\times_k\bar X$ be correspondences of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-trf-correspondence]. Their fixed diagrams [def-trf-fixed-scheme] have objects $X,X\times X,C,F=\operatorname{Fix}(c),s$ and arrows the identities, structure maps $a_Z$, projections $p_i$, $c,c_i$, diagonals $\Delta$, fixed inclusions $i_F$, fixed projections $d$, and $ci_F=\Delta d$; barred symbols denote the corresponding objects and arrows for $\bar c$. Work in the finite-Tor constructible categories with the specified ordinary and exceptional adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility] and the normalized geometric operation datum of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. The categories are the finite-Tor full subcategories of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], on the small pro-etale sites specified by the coefficient conventions. All operations below are derived. Their restrictions, including internal Hom and Verdier duality, use the preservation statements of [thm-sf-ctf-stability], at the finite stage only. Pullback tensor, unit, signed symmetry and composition identifications are the canonical ones of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso, lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition].

A cohomological pre-comparison is the following data: functors $f_Z$, natural transformations $t_Z$, $\alpha_g$, $\beta_g$, and a specified isomorphism $\iota$, of types
$$f_Z:D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)\to D^b_{ctf}(\bar Z,A),\quad t_Z:f_ZM\otimes f_ZN\to f_Z(M\otimes N),\quad\alpha_g:\bar g^*f_V\to f_Ug^*,\quad\beta_g:f_Ug^!\to\bar g^!f_V,\quad\iota:f_sA_s\xrightarrow{\sim}A_s$$
for each diagram object $Z$ and each listed diagram arrow $g:U\to V$, with $M,N\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ for $t_Z$. The listed objects and arrows are regarded as labelled diagram entries, even when two of their underlying schemes or morphisms coincide, with one exception: since $s$ is terminal in both diagrams, the structure arrow $a_s$ and the identity $\operatorname{id}_s$ are one entry, so $\alpha_{a_s}=\alpha_{\operatorname{id}_s}$ and $\beta_{a_s}=\beta_{\operatorname{id}_s}$. In (III), a composite is listed when it is a listed entry by the identities of the fixed diagram, which hold for every correspondence (such as $p_i\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$, $p_ic=c_i$ and $a_Vg=a_U$ for $g:U\to V$). Put $\omega_Z=Ra_Z^!A_s$ and $D_ZM=R\mathcal Hom(M,\omega_Z)$ [def-trf-dualizing-complex]. Define $\delta_Z:f_Z\omega_Z\to\omega_{\bar Z}$ by $\beta_{a_Z}$ followed by $a_{\bar Z}^!\iota$. Define $r_Z:f_ZR\mathcal Hom(M,N)\to R\mathcal Hom(f_ZM,f_ZN)$ as the tensor–internal-Hom transpose [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction, lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] of $f_ZR\mathcal Hom(M,N)\otimes f_ZM\xrightarrow{t_Z}f_Z(R\mathcal Hom(M,N)\otimes M)\xrightarrow{f_Z\operatorname{ev}}f_ZN$, and $d_Z:f_ZD_ZM\to D_{\bar Z}f_ZM$ as $r_Z$ followed by postcomposition with $\delta_Z$.

Use the ordinary counit $\varepsilon_g:g^*Rg_*\to\operatorname{id}$ and the exceptional unit $\eta_g:\operatorname{id}\to g^!Rg_!$ from [def-trf-admissibility]. The mate convention is [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. The ordinary mate $\alpha_{g,*}:f_VRg_*\to R\bar g_*f_U$ is defined by transposing $\bar g^*f_VRg_*\xrightarrow{\alpha_g}f_Ug^*Rg_*\xrightarrow{f_U\varepsilon_g}f_U$. The exceptional mate $\beta_{g,!}:R\bar g_!f_U\to f_VRg_!$ is defined by transposing $f_U\xrightarrow{f_U\eta_g}f_Ug^!Rg_!\xrightarrow{\beta_g} \bar g^!f_VRg_!$.

A pre-comparison is compactifiable when it satisfies the following seven requirements. (I) Each $t_Z$ is commutative (with the signed tensor symmetry) and associative. (II) $\iota\circ t_s=\iota\otimes\iota$ on $f_sA_s\otimes f_sA_s$, with the unit identifications inserted. (III) $\alpha_{\operatorname{id}}=\operatorname{id}$ and, for composable listed arrows $g:U\to V$, $h:V\to W$ whose composite is listed, $\alpha_{hg}=(\alpha_g h^*)\circ(\bar g^*\alpha_h)$ under the pullback compositors. (IV) Ordinary comparison respects tensor: $\alpha_g(M\otimes N)\circ\bar g^*t_V=t_U\circ(\alpha_g(M)\otimes\alpha_g(N))$. (V) Each evaluation-defined $d_Z$ is an isomorphism. (VI) If both $g$ and $\bar g$ are proper, then $\alpha_{g,*}$ and $\beta_{g,!}$ are inverse isomorphisms, under $Rg_!=Rg_*$ and $R\bar g_!=R\bar g_*$. (VII) There exist proper $k$-schemes $X^*,C^*,\bar X^*,\bar C^*$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], dense open immersions $u_X:X\hookrightarrow X^*$, $u_C:C\hookrightarrow C^*$ and their barred counterparts [def-weil-open-immersion], and correspondences $c^*:C^*\to X^*\times_kX^*$, $\bar c^*:\bar C^*\to\bar X^*\times_k\bar X^*$ with
$$c^*u_C=(u_X\times u_X)c,\qquad \bar c^*u_{\bar C}=(u_{\bar X}\times u_{\bar X})\bar c.$$
Dense means that the image is dense in the underlying topological space. The resulting compactified fixed diagrams have induced open immersions $u_Z:Z\hookrightarrow Z^*$, including $u_{X\times X}=u_X\times u_X$, the induced fixed-scheme open immersion, and $u_s=\operatorname{id}_s$; use analogous notation for the barred diagram. There is a pre-comparison $(f_Z^*,t_Z^*,\alpha_g^*,\beta_g^*,\iota^*)$ on these compactified diagrams satisfying (I)--(VI), together with natural isomorphisms
$$\rho_Z:f_Z\,u_Z^*\xrightarrow{\sim}u_{\bar Z}^*\,f_Z^*.$$
The restriction identifications use pullback composition, the exceptional composition of [def-trf-admissibility], and the open-immersion adjunction $u_!\dashv u^*$ of [prop-exc-open-adjoint], identifying $u^!$ with $u^*$ as right adjoints to $u_!$. Under these canonical restriction identifications, $\rho_Z$ identifies the tensor maps $t_Z$ with the restrictions of $t_Z^*$ and identifies $\alpha_g,\beta_g$ with the restrictions of $\alpha_g^*,\beta_g^*$; at $s$ it identifies $\iota$ with $\iota^*$. Here the superscript $*$ on $f_Z^*,t_Z^*,\alpha_g^*,\beta_g^*$ labels the compactified data, not a pullback operation.

A cohomological comparison is a finite composite of compactifiable pre-comparisons. For successive pre-comparisons $f:c\to\bar c$ and $e:\bar c\to\widehat c$, composition has functors $e_{\bar Z}f_Z$, tensor maps $e(t^f_Z)\circ t^e_{\bar Z}$, ordinary maps $e(\alpha^f_g)\circ(\alpha^e_{\bar g}f_V)$, exceptional maps $(\beta^e_{\bar g}f_V)\circ e(\beta^f_g)$, and coefficient isomorphism $\iota^e\circ e_s(\iota^f)$. A composite of length zero is the identity pre-comparison. Intermediate correspondences and coefficient categories have the same conventions. Also write
$$j_Z:A_{\bar Z}\xrightarrow{\sim}a_{\bar Z}^*A_s\xrightarrow{a_{\bar Z}^*(\iota^{-1})}a_{\bar Z}^*f_sA_s\xrightarrow{\alpha_{a_Z}(A_s)}f_Za_Z^*A_s=f_ZA_Z,\qquad h_Z(q)=f_Z(q)\circ j_Z\quad(q:A_Z\to M),$$
and, for external products as in [def-trf-external-product],
$$\Pi_{M,N}:f_XM\boxtimes f_XN\xrightarrow{\alpha_{p_1}\otimes\alpha_{p_2}}f_{X\times X}p_1^*M\otimes f_{X\times X}p_2^*N\xrightarrow{t_{X\times X}}f_{X\times X}(M\boxtimes N).$$
These definitions prescribe maps; they do not assert trace compatibility.

from.place: Proof paragraph (1) and (2): specialization to the normal cone; structural comparison datum used to prove Proposition 1.3.5

split_report.summary: Definition-only split, with no new nodes. Read Varshavsky Notation 1.1.2(c), §§4.1.1--4.1.3 and Notation 4.2.3 against all clauses; restored dense open compactifications and specified restriction isomorphisms and composition. Named the existing finite-Tor preservation, monoidal pullback, derived currying and mate ingredients so all displayed maps have their prescribed domains. No matching project declaration or Mathlib definition was found.
split_report.blueprint: The comparison datum makes precise the specialization-to-the-normal-cone ingredient in the proof of lem-trf-local-term-locality, through lem-trf-trace-specialization, as recorded in blueprint.from. The item is an auxiliary definition, not the key statement of sk-i-curve-zero, so its unit realization is unchanged.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NF-d713d1d0b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: Varshavsky math/0505564 §0.2-0.3, Notation 1.1.2(c)/Rem 1.1.3 (pp.6-7), §4.1.1, Notation 4.1.2, Def 4.1.3, Ex 4.1.4 (pp.25-28), Notation 4.2.3/Lemma 4.2.4 (p.32); all 17 stmt_deps statements, the citers lem-trf-trace-specialization, lem-trf-specialization-cohomological-comparison, lem-trf-cohomological-evaluation/exchange-calculus and lem-trf-specialization-external-product, and the unit sk-i-curve-zero. These parts match the source: the data types; delta/r/d (4.1.1(c)(i)-(iii)); both mates against def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate (the ordinary one is the mate, the exceptional one the inverse-mate formula; directions as in BC^*_g and BC^!_g); composition (4.1.1(d)); axioms (I)-(VI); (VII) with dominant=dense compactifications and a single u_X (the worker's density repair is correct: the two-point example checks out); Fix(c) is open in Fix(c^*) because X×X→X^*×X^* is mono; rho_Z restriction data as in 4.1.2(b); and j_Z with iota^{-1} and Pi as in 4.2.3. Every operation is typed by thm-sf-ctf-stability (i)-(vi) at the finite stage, and u^!=u^* comes from prop-exc-open-adjoint. The coefficient category is the project's A_{E,n} pro-etale D^b_ctf, with no change of coefficients. Edge cases tested: identity comparison, empty schemes, n=1 and n>1, nonproper g, already proper diagrams, and X=s. No new nodes. The duplicate searches over the DAG and the blueprint found nothing. No SGA citation, no tool_uses. One repaired fault (E1/E6, def weaker than source): making every arrow a labelled entry separated a_s from id_s. In the source these are one element (pi_pt=Id_pt), and keeping them apart left alpha_{a_s} and beta_{a_s} unconstrained, which affects j_s, delta_s and Lemma 4.2.4(b) as used by the evaluation calculus. The fix is in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula/def-trf-cohomological-comparison.json and changes only the statement: it now says a_s and id_s are one entry, and that a composite in (III) is listed when the identities of the formal fixed diagram make it a listed entry. Details are in review.md.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
